Build a regular service-hour pathway

People who list service hours as an interest could benefit from a regular volunteering pathway. A school partnership is a route to explore.

·
Why this connects

A useful next step: Ask whether a regular shift would help, then check approval, supervision, and hour-recording requirements with a school coordinator.

These illustrative stated interests do not establish school approval or agreement to participate.

components.html:
Make service hours a reason to come back

Propose four weekly, two-hour garden shifts with a named supervisor and a record of completed hours.

Why it could help A clear route to contribute regularly. School recognition depends on each person’s requirements and school approval.

  1. Ask which people are students, their deadlines and any confirmed hour targets.
  2. Agree school approval and supervision, then offer a repeatable shift.
See the basis

These are proposed activities. Interest matches do not establish participation or eligibility. Check the school partnership’s terms before making an offer.

3 of 5

32 h

narrative.overview:
Roots is a deep-green intelligence workspace. Overview retains a 680px reading column with connected findings, inspectable evidence, and a composer beneath. People Groups and Opportunities use 1000px open paired rows: practical narrative on the left, clickable avatar clusters and recorded evidence on the right, stacked on mobile. Self-hosted DM Sans, light text, pale sage actions, native disclosures, and fine dividers keep the interface calm.

People begins with Ways to take part, grounded in five service-hour-interest profiles and eight one-visit profiles in the seed. Students, employer connections, and confirmed targets appear only when explicit facts are recorded. Opportunities begins with Participation ideas: proposed supervised service shifts, practical in-kind support, and learning with a follow-up visit. A separately sourced Microsoft employee-giving policy remains visible without inventing employee matches. Everyone preserves the table, and All leads, Projects, and Saved preserve the library.
keyCharacteristics: Overview stays at 680px; only People Groups and Opportunities widen to 1000px.
Open paired rows place narratives beside profile clusters and recorded evidence, then stack at 760px.
Practical activities, possible benefits, and proposed next steps precede source detail.
Twelve leads comprise eleven conceptual candidates and one sourced public policy.
rules: Ways to take part is the People Groups default; Interests, Participation, Age groups, and Everyone remain available.
Only explicit profile fields or saved overrides establish student, school, or employer context. Clearing returns a value to unknown; other saved preferences and notes survive.
Confirmed target cohorts use locally recorded hour targets and exclude illustrative targets. Recorded total hours do not prove approved school progress.
Participation ideas uses deterministic ordering; Most people and Closest match retain their distinct documented formulas. Funding & support never ranks projected income.
The Microsoft policy checked 24 October 2026 states $25 per eligible volunteer hour within a combined $15,000 annual match cap. Public policy does not establish Roots or employee eligibility.
Keep the separate Microsoft row visible throughout For your community, including Funding & support. Show employee avatars only for an explicit employer record.
Keep the Microsoft external-source check separate from browser-local observation/check timestamps. Check again does not search the web.
dos: Use actual group counts, direct recorded hours, and valid visit totals, noting missing-data coverage.
Clarify that gardening’s eight of 35 identifies people who named that interest.
Use named accessible avatar buttons and a complete-members entry point.
Link official Microsoft policy and its FY25 nonprofit guide; explain Benevity, an eligible employee or Change Agent, and employee-submitted hour requests.
donts: Do not infer students, employers, ages, support needs, school requirements, or willingness from interests, names, email, or hours.
Do not present proposals as booked activities, secured benefits, retention predictions, or projected revenue.
Do not change Overview into the paired layout or restore invented monthly trends.
